hyps.why: At very small learning rates the network is badly undertrained in 243 epochs, so a larger step size gives a big gain.
Near lr 0.08 to 1 Adam becomes unstable or diverges, so going higher hurts.
Lowering an excessively large learning rate restores stable training.
With a small learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and even stronger undertraining.
More updates per epoch compensate for the small step size.
Small batches combined with a large learning rate give noisy, unstable updates.
Wider networks fit faster at a given small learning rate, which reduces undertraining.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units at high learning rates.
An L2 penalty approaching 1 over-regularizes and underfits.
Narrow networks have little spare capacity, so extra weight decay causes underfitting.
